title: Hankyung: five South Korean savings banks, now including Hana, hit by hacking since late September
date_note: Hankyung's article of 24 November is the only source; the individual intrusions are not dated here beyond the article's own wording.
org: South Korean savings banks (Hana, OK, Welcome, DB, Yegaram)
geo_basis: country named in the source; no city given, pin at Seoul
summary: Hankyung reports that five savings banks (Yegaram, Welcome, DB, OK and Hana) have been hit by hacking since late September, according to its tally. For Hana, it says identity-verification data including names, resident registration numbers, phone numbers and addresses was exposed; a Hana official said the bank blocked the IP addresses involved. SBS Biz reported on 13 October that the FSS began on-site inspections of Yegaram and Welcome.
plain: Hankyung reports five South Korean savings banks have been hacked since late September. Hana Savings Bank says it has blocked the IP addresses involved and is monitoring around the clock.
exec: Hankyung's tally of five hacked savings banks shows customer identity data at smaller Korean lenders is being exposed through web-linked services.

validation.note: Hankyung (24 Nov) is the only page stating the five-bank tally and the Hana intrusion; SBS Biz (13 Oct) separately reports the Yegaram and Welcome hacks and the FSS inspection but does not mention Hana Savings Bank. No bank notice was read.

review.note: Compared title, five banks, Hana system, data types and statement with Hankyung; single_source ok
